archetype.name: Pocket Passer (short-area volume)
archetype.definition: A second-year rim-of-the-pocket thrower who wins with timing and accuracy underneath and over the middle, carries a pass-heavy offense on volume, and adds value by scrambling rather than by designed runs.

report.headline: Accurate, competent volume passer whose season now hinges on a crumbling pocket
report.take:
Shough is a better quarterback than his 6.22 yards per attempt (35th of 55) suggests, and a worse one than his 239.5 passing yards a game (14th) suggests. The truth sits in the middle: his 0.008 EPA per dropback ranks 27th but sits 0.034 above the qualifier average, and his completion rate runs 3.8 points over the league mark. He is a rhythm passer who lives inside 20 yards. His 203 short attempts produced 0.166 EPA a play with 12 of his 16 TDs. His 73 intermediate throws were his best area at 0.264 EPA. The middle of the field (0.277 EPA, +5.3 CPOE) is where he looks most comfortable. Volume comes from a defense that ranks 22nd in EPA and dead last against deep passes. That keeps the Saints throwing: their pass rate over expected ranks 7th.

What drags his rate stats down is not mostly his arm. Throws at or behind the line of scrimmage, 64 of them, cost 23 points of EPA at -0.359 a play with a -11.7 CPOE. That is a screen and swing-pass game that has failed. It is a scheme-and-blocking problem stacked on top of him, and it is why his overall yards per attempt trails his depth-by-depth efficiency. Strip it out and he has been an above-average distributor. Olave (0.335 EPA per target on 101 targets) and Vele (0.343) are both producing.

The real flaws are ball security and, lately, sacks. Four lost fumbles ranks last among 55 qualifiers, and the charting has him at nine turnover-worthy fumbles. That is a habit, not bad luck. Over the last three games his sack rate jumped to 11.1%, 4.1 points above his season rate. He took 14 sacks and his EPA per dropback went negative, even as his CPOE (+0.4) actually ticked up. He is still putting the ball where it should go; he just isn't getting the chance often enough. His time to throw crept to 3.05 against Chicago. Now right tackle Taliese Fuaga, center Erik McCoy and tackle Asim Richards are all listed out. That is the variable that matters most.

Year over year, he has traded some efficiency (YPA down 1.07, CPOE down 2) for a more aggressive, cleaner-throwing version. Bad throws are down 2.3 points and tight-window attempts are up. His pressure-to-sack rate improved from 48th of 62 a year ago to 21st of 45. That last gain is what the current line situation threatens to erase.

strengths.title: Efficient short and intermediate passing
strengths.body: His 0-9 yard throws run at 0.166 EPA with a 75.4% completion rate and +4.2 CPOE. The 10-19 yard window is even better at 0.264 EPA. That is timing and placement, not scheme spoon-feeding, and it has held across a 10-game sample with real volume. It is the stable core of his game.

strengths.title: Red-zone finishing
strengths.body: He has 14 touchdowns against one interception inside the 20, with a +10 CPOE there. That is why his TDs per game rose 0.6 from last year despite worse yardage efficiency. The accuracy is real, but red-zone TD rates swing on small samples (51 plays), so expect it to cool somewhat.

strengths.title: Scrambles that pay
strengths.body: His 22 scrambles average 0.386 EPA, and 10 went for first downs. That makes them a genuine bailout when the pocket breaks. Designed runs are the opposite: -0.31 EPA and a 50% stuff rate. His rushing value comes from improvisation, not the playbook.

concerns.title: Sacks spiking behind a depleted line
concerns.body: Fourteen sacks in three games pushed his recent sack rate to 11.1%, and his EPA per dropback in that stretch fell to -0.058. Chicago got him six times while he held the ball 3.05 seconds. Three linemen are now listed out, including Fuaga and McCoy, who played 100% and 97% of snaps. This is the most likely thing to sink his next few games, and it is largely outside his control.

concerns.title: Fumbles are a pattern
concerns.body: He has four lost fumbles, ranking last among 55 qualifiers, and nine turnover-worthy fumbles. A rising sack count only feeds this. It is a real flaw in pocket ball handling, not variance, and it caps how much a coaching staff can trust him in late, close spots.

concerns.title: Dead screen game deflates YPA
concerns.body: His 64 throws at or behind the line have cost 23 EPA at a 23.4% success rate. That is the main reason his yards per attempt fell 1.07 from last season. It is more design and blocking than him, but it sits on his line every week until Kellen Moore fixes or abandons it.

trend.note: After an efficient stretch around the Ravens and Steelers games, the last three weeks have turned negative: -7.3 passing EPA, 14 sacks, and only one TD a game. He has also added more scramble yardage. The accuracy held; the protection didn't.

nextGame.headline: Heavy underdog in Cincinnati: volume likely, efficiency at risk
nextGame.body:
The Book has Cincinnati -10 with a 50.5 total. The Bengals' offense ranks 2nd in EPA and 1st in pass rate over expected. That points to Shough trailing and throwing a lot. This defense gives up yardage to quarterbacks (273.2 a game, 28th) but not touchdowns (1.3, 5th). It is soft underneath (short-pass EPA 22nd) and strong deep (6th), which fits his short-to-intermediate game. The catch: when he trails by 9+, his EPA has been -0.055 a play, so the volume tends to come with empty yards.

Availability is the story on his side. Fuaga, McCoy and Richards are all listed out as of the 23rd, with return estimates of game day; treat that as uncertain. Against a defense with a 7.4% sack rate (10th), a patched line is a real sack-and-fumble risk. Juwan Johnson is questionable with a hamstring and still being evaluated. That matters because Cincinnati has been beaten by tight ends (TE1s score 4.3 PPR over their averages, 30th), and Johnson has been his third-best target. Cincinnati is missing CB Jalen Davis, but he has only played three games, so it changes little.

keyMatchups.title: Short game vs soft underneath coverage
keyMatchups.body: Cincinnati allows 0.066 EPA on short passes (22nd) while ranking 6th against deep throws. That steers Shough toward the 0-19 yard throws he already does best, where Olave and Vele have both been above 0.33 EPA per target.

keyMatchups.title: Patched line vs Bengals rush
keyMatchups.body: Without three listed linemen, his recent sack problem meets a pass rush sacking on 7.4% of dropbacks. Third downs are already where it breaks: 12 sacks and -0.088 EPA there.

keyMatchups.title: Shootout script
keyMatchups.body: Cincinnati's passing offense (0.253 EPA, 2nd) against a Saints pass defense that is last against deep balls should put New Orleans behind early. That means attempts, not necessarily efficiency.

nextGame.watch: How many of the three listed linemen actually play. With them, expect 250-plus yards of rhythm passing; without them, expect another four-sack, fumble-risk afternoon.

restOfSeason.body:
The volume is safe. A bad defense and a pass-leaning staff keep him near 37-39 attempts. I'd project 215-260 passing yards a game with a touchdown or a bit more. The red-zone touchdown rate should cool toward normal, which trims TDs slightly from his first-half pace. His short and intermediate efficiency and his accuracy have held all year and should keep holding.

The swing is protection. If the line returns intact, his sack rate should settle back toward his season level, and his EPA should drift back above league average, where it spent most of the year. If the injuries linger, the last three weeks are the template: lots of sacks, scramble yardage up, and a fumble problem that gets worse with every hit. Rushing should stay in the 15-35 range, mostly from scrambles.
swingFactors: Fixing or cutting the screen game

confidence.note: Ten full starts make his passing profile reliable. Offensive-line availability is unknown week to week.
